newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money at 3.00/3.05 pct with firm tinge.
newsitem.headline: German call money at 3.00/3.05 pct with firm tinge.

text.p: German call money rates were traded in a range of 3.00 to 3.05 percent on Thursday, but dealers said the market had a firmer edge to it.
Players said that by mid-morning trade, it was becoming difficult to execute trades at rates under the 3.02 percent level.

With effective deposits by commercial banks at the Bundesbank falling on Wednesday to 42.1 billion marks from 42.9 billion marks on Tuesday, traders said rates could tighten up as the weekend approaches.
"Today's activity is all part of the normal process of shifting funds and reserves," said one trader in Frankfurt.

Average reserves held at the Bundesbank for the month through Wednesday totalled 41.1 billion marks, up from 41.0 billion marks previously. Reserves were above the preliminary minimum reserve requirement of 39.6 billion marks, announced by the Bundesbank on Wednesday.
Bank borrowing from the Lombard facility was negligible. The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average (FIONA) rate was quoted at 3.07425 compared with 3.07083 percent on Wednesday.
